_note: Corrections for rows the Taiwan sheet records awkwardly, keyed by its product id. `id` replaces a placeholder product code, `nameEn` supplies a title, and `blade` says which blade the row really is so it shares that blade's tournament record instead of looking untested. `skip` drops a row that is not a blade at all — the sheet files a set's leftover loose parts as blade rows named after the product, and they would otherwise sit in the tier list as phantom blades wearing a photo of a bit. Use it only where the row describes no blade; the parts themselves are described in setContents.json. `assist` / `overblade` backfill an in-the-box part the sheet leaves off: `assist` fills a blank assist column, `overblade` supplies the CX Expand Blade over blade (single-letter code, defined in manualParts.json) the sheet has no column for at all. `duplicateOf` drops a row that is a second listing of a part already in the sheet under another casing, naming the row it merges into. The sheet carries `Nr` beside `NR` and `Op` beside `OP` — one physical bit each, listed twice from two authoring passes: the `NR`/`OP` rows carry a pasted screenshot, the `Nr`/`Op` rows a re-hosted retail product photo (BT-PRD-*.webp). Nobody re-graded anything; the rows simply disagree, `NR` at A against `Nr` at S, and `Op` has no grade at all. Keep the uppercase row: it is the casing the tournament feed writes, so the record joins without an alias, and forCode() already reaches the lowercase key that partSpecs.json and creatorPicks.json use. Without this, the two rows blend separately and disagree — `Nr` scored 80 on its sheet grade alone and, having no tournament record, was capped to A+, while `NR` blended its 73 placements down to A. `Op` is dropped today only because it has no grade, which is luck rather than design: grade it in the sheet and a second Operate appears.
_over_blades: Only the four confirmed CX Expand Blade families ship an over blade (Bahamut Blitz→Break B, Ragna Rage→Flow F, Unicorn Delta→Peak P, Brachio Whip→Outer O); every other CX blade uses the original three-part Main Blade system and gets none. The blank assist columns on the CX random-booster rows (e.g. CX-05-04, CX-08-04, CX-11-02, CX-17-03) are deliberately left blank: those are UX/BX blades, which have no assist blade — filling them would be wrong.
